title: Add minimality-driven regression guard CI hook
author: Nadia Park
release_notes: Introduce a minimality-driven CI hook that detects when candidate model versions require more prompt context to produce the same outputs (minimality regressions) and gates merges when those regressions co-occur with quality drops. Opt-in via CI YAML; supports soft-fail and auto-quarantine modes.
description: Motivation: Some model updates subtly change how much context they require to produce the same answer; that increases serving cost and can surface regressions in prompt engineering. This PR adds a 'minimality' regression guard CI hook that measures the fewest-prefix length required to reproduce a baseline response on a set of representative prompt-sets and raises a signal when the minimal prefix length grows significantly. Design: 1) minimality metric: for each prompt + ground-truth target, run a binary-prefix-reduction probe against the candidate model to find the smallest prefix (in tokens) that still yields the same high-confidence top result as the baseline anchor. 2) baseline snapshots: store per-prompt anchor minimality (token count) in the eval datastore; snapshots are versioned alongside existing prompt-set baselines. 3) metric aggregation: compute minimality_delta = candidate_minimality - anchor_minimality per prompt; report distribution (median, 90th percentile, fraction > threshold). 4) gating rules: by default the hook only blocks merges when (a) median minimality_delta > 1.0 tokens AND (b) a related quality metric (e.g., exact_match, accuracy) drops by > 1.5% — this avoids false positives where a small minimality shift is acceptable in exchange for quality. 5) modes: soft-fail (annotates PR and raises issue but does not block), strict (block on rule), and auto-quarantine (move candidate to canary lane if threshold exceeded). Implementation summary: - eval_harness/metrics/minimality.py: core probe + stable-comparison logic (with configurable similarity heuristics: token-equality, normalized-utterance-match, semantic-similarity threshold). - eval_harness/hooks/minimality_guard.py: CI adapter that pulls baseline snapshots, runs sampled minimality probes against candidate artifact, computes aggregated signal, and posts results to PR and CI annotations. - ci/configs/minimality-hook.yaml: opt-in CI job template with sampling config, time budget, and gating thresholds. - tests/test_minimality.py: unit and integration tests using a lightweight local model stub. Backwards compatibility: Hook is opt-in; teams enable it by adding the YAML into their repo's CI folder. Checklist: [x] Add metric impl and unit tests; [x] CI adapter and job template; [x] Docs and example prompt-sets; [x] Add baseline snapshot writer for anchor creation; [x] Add smoke-run to pipeline. How to run locally: ./scripts/local_run_minimality.sh --prompt-set examples/prompt-sets/minimality_demo.json --sample-size 100 --mode dry-run Expected behaviour: runs sample probes, writes a minimality_report.json in artifacts, exits non-zero only in strict mode when gating conditions met. Performance: the probe uses a tokenized binary search and supports reusing KV-cache for prefix-only runs; typical overhead is ~1.2x of a standard smoke-eval for the same sample size. Testing performed: ran full smoke-eval (n=250) against main anchor + a synthetic candidate that intentionally required longer context; observed median minimality_delta = 0.9 tokens, 90th percentile = 3.4 tokens, fraction >2 tokens = 11%. In strict mode combined with a 2.1% drop in accuracy, the hook flagged the candidate. Rollout plan: land in eval-harness main, publish the ci template; coordinate with platform teams to add opt-in to redwood and redwood-examples. Metrics and dashboards: the CI job writes summarised telemetry to eval telemetry pipeline (metric names: minimality.delta.median, minimality.delta.p90, minimality.regression_fraction) and emits a trace span for probe time. Security/Cost: probes run under same tenant credentials as other eval jobs; sampling defaults reduce cost. See docs/eval-hooks/minimality.md for full operator guide.
commits_summary: c1a2b3: add minimality metric and comparator; d4e5f6: CI adapter and YAML; 9a8b7c: tests and docs; squash -> final implement with minor lint fixes
review_comments: Marco Ruiz (reviewer): Nice direction. A few items: (1) need clearer defn of 'same top result' — how tolerant to whitespace/normalization? (2) sampling config should default to small to avoid CI timeouts. Action: please add normalization step and update CI defaults.

Author (Nadia Park): Added normalization pipeline (strip/normalize Unicode, collapse whitespace) and semantic fallback using cosine similarity when token-equality fails. Default sample-size lowered to 100 for CI job; full-run remains configurable.
Evelyn Chen (reviewer): Can we make the gating check composable with other gates (e.g., latency/perf)? Also add an opt-out annotation for noisy prompt-sets.
Author (Nadia Park): Hook now emits a composite signal label and supports @ci:skip-minimality PR annotation to opt-out for noisy prompt-sets. Documentation updated.
Priya Nair (reviewer): Tests look good; can we add a tiny integration run on a real model in the smoke pipeline?
Author (Nadia Park): Added a smoke-eval integration run using the internal small-checkpoint model; job included in CI matrix.
discussion_summary: Consensus: minimality is a useful orthogonal signal to quality; keep conservative defaults and soft-fail as the rollout path. Platform teams will opt-in per repo. Reviewers requested normalization, opt-out annotation, and reduced default sampling; all addressed.
